subsystems.name: Spatial light modulator (SLM) array
subsystems.role: modulates light to form the holographic interference pattern that reconstructs the 3D image.

subsystems.name: Illumination
subsystems.role: provides coherent or partially coherent light that the SLM can shape.
parts: red, green and blue laser diodes

subsystems.name: Optical relay and steering
subsystems.role: directs the modulated light to the viewer's eyes and expands the viewing zone.

subsystems.name: Hologram rendering pipeline
subsystems.role: computes the interference pattern from a 3D scene in real time.
parts: hologram computation algorithms (e.g. point-cloud or layer-based)

subsystems.name: Eye tracking
subsystems.role: tracks the viewer's pupil positions to adapt the hologram and reduce computational load.

subsystems.name: Housing and thermal management
subsystems.role: keeps the precise optical alignment stable and components within operating temperature.

buildSteps.title: Specify the optical design
buildSteps.detail: Choose target resolution, viewing angle, physical size and colour gamut; these set the required SLM pixel count, laser wavelengths and optical path length.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the SLM panels
buildSteps.detail: High-resolution phase modulators are made on silicon backplanes using liquid-crystal-on-silicon (LCOS) or micro-electromechanical (MEMS) processes, then packaged with driver chips.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the light engine
buildSteps.detail: Red, green and blue laser diodes are collimated, combined into a single beam and directed to the SLM with beam-shaping optics.

buildSteps.title: Align the optical train
buildSteps.detail: The SLM, relay lenses, mirrors and steering elements are mounted and aligned to micron tolerances so the reconstructed wavefront is correct.

buildSteps.title: Develop the rendering hardware and software
buildSteps.detail: Real-time hologram computation is implemented on GPUs or FPGAs, using algorithms that convert 3D scene data into phase patterns at kilohertz rates.

buildSteps.title: Integrate eye tracking
buildSteps.detail: Cameras and infrared illuminators are positioned to capture pupil positions, and the rendering pipeline is adapted to update the hologram only for the observed eye locations.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and test
buildSteps.detail: The assembled display is calibrated to correct optical aberrations, then tested for image quality, viewing angle, colour accuracy and user comfort.

buildSteps.title: Package into a desktop unit
buildSteps.detail: The optics, electronics and cooling are fitted into a monitor-like enclosure with standard video interfaces and ergonomic adjustments.

prerequisites.why: current SLMs have too few pixels and too slow refresh rates to produce wide-angle, real-time holograms at desktop scale.

prerequisites.tech: Real-time hologram computation algorithms and hardware
prerequisites.why: rendering a full-colour hologram from a complex 3D scene requires enormous computing power that is only now becoming feasible.
laser diodes are mature, but further cost reduction and size shrinking are needed for consumer desktop products.
eye tracking is used in virtual-reality headsets, but must be integrated with hologram rendering to expand the viewing zone.
driving millions of SLM pixels at kilohertz rates demands data links faster than current display standards.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes demonstrate small, monochrome or limited-colour holographic displays with narrow viewing angles.
pathway.unlocks: proof that light-field reconstruction without glasses is possible in a desktop form factor.

pathway.milestone: improved SLMs and algorithms enable desktop-sized prototypes with acceptable resolution, colour and real-time performance.
pathway.unlocks: use in design review and medical imaging, where depth cues matter.

pathway.milestone: integration of eye tracking and optical steering yields wider viewing zones and support for multiple viewers.
commercial products with full colour, high resolution and comfortable viewing angles reach the market.
pathway.unlocks: replacement of conventional monitors for tasks that benefit from true 3D visuals.
